Place seeds for a Voronoi tessellation

Source: R/seeding.R
get_voronoi_seeds.Rd

Creates an sf POINT layer of seed locations, one per cell of the Voronoi tessellation built on them: k-means centres of a cloud of points, points drawn uniformly inside a boundary, or points you provide.

Usage

get_voronoi_seeds(
  boundary = NULL,
  method = c("kmeans", "random", "provided"),
  n = NULL,
  seeds = NULL,
  sample_points = NULL,
  kmeans_nstart = NULL,
  kmeans_iter = 100,
  set_seed = NULL,
  partition = c("density", "kmeans"),
  init = NULL,
  density_power = 1,
  density_k = 8
)

Arguments

boundary

Optional polygonal sf object defining the sampling area. Rows without a location, rows the repair leaves without a polygon, vertices at a latitude beyond 90 and mixed dimensions are handled as "Boundaries" in spatialkit-geometry says; "Sampling inside the boundary" gives how points are drawn in it.

method

How to place the seeds: "kmeans" (default; cluster centres of sample_points, or of points drawn in boundary), "random" (uniform in boundary) or "provided" (the points in seeds).

n

Integer; number of seeds to return. Required for method = "kmeans" and method = "random". Ignored for method = "provided", where every row of seeds is returned; a mismatch between n and nrow(seeds) is reported as a warning.

For method = "kmeans" it is an upper bound only: k-means cannot produce more centres than there are distinct positions in the sampling cloud, nor as many centres as there are rows. When n exceeds either ceiling it is clamped, with a warning naming the count used. Asking for as many seeds as there are points (n = nrow(sample_points)) gives nrow(sample_points) - 1. Check nrow() on the result; do not assume n.

Besides a number, n accepts what the level-selection step returned: the integer vector of ranked candidates from determine_optimal_levels() (its first element is used; its NA is refused with a note on where it came from), a select_resolution() result (its $best), or a resolution_profile(). A profile built without an estimate is read with select_resolution() by cp. A profile built with estimate is read by criterion = "auto", the rule that goes with its estimate: a size for pooled values and the lowest leave-one-out error for plain means. The size is the profile's own when it was built at one, and 4.5 rows per cell otherwise, and the count is the profile's level for that size, or the built level nearest to max(2, round(n / obs_per_cell)) when the profile has none for it (with a warning of class "spatialkit_size_not_reached"). select_resolution(profile) with no criterion reads such a profile the same way, since its default criterion is "auto". A profile built with obs_per_cell and without an estimate is read by cp like any profile without one; pass select_resolution(profile, criterion = "size") for the count its size gives. The result then carries attr(, "n_from") saying which. A count read off a selection or a profile comes with what the selection found: a warning of class "spatialkit_bound_chosen" when the optimum sits on a bound of the ladder, so the bound chose the count, and one of class "spatialkit_no_structure" when one cell for the whole layer scores as well. A count set by a size has no optimum, so no bound can choose it; its "spatialkit_no_structure" warning says that the count stands and that the cell values will say little that one mean does not. A profile without an estimate and with no cp to read is an error (class "spatialkit_no_default_criterion" when another criterion is finite); see resolution_profile().

With method = "kmeans", a selection or profile also carries the centres of the partition the profile scored at that count, and those are returned instead of a new k-means: a k-means partition, weighted or not, is the Voronoi partition of its centres, so their cells are the cells the criteria judged. On a profile without an estimate whose centres were fitted to a subsample, select_resolution() refits them to every point first, and those centres are returned, with attr(, "refit"): their cells are near the cells judged but not the same. sample_points, when given, is then only assigned to them (for attr(, "kmeans")) and gives the cover, and boundary only sets the CRS and the cover; kmeans_nstart, kmeans_iter and set_seed are not used, and neither are partition, init and the density settings: the centres are of the kind the profile was built with, and naming another here is a warning of class "spatialkit_partition_unused". A call names what it supplies: a partition or an init passed in the call; with partition = "density" passed, both density settings at their values, defaults included; without it, a density setting other than its default. A call that supplies none of the four is told nothing, whichever kind and settings the profile was built with. Pass the count as a number (n = sel$best) for a fresh k-means instead.

seeds

sf POINT object of user-provided seeds (method = "provided"). Methods "kmeans" and "random" do not read it, and ignore it with a warning; so does a call that passes seed =, which R matches to seeds (the seed of the random stream is set_seed). Seeds in another CRS than boundary are returned in the boundary's CRS; seeds that mix XY and XYZ (or XYM) points are then returned in XY, with a warning of class "spatialkit_zm_dropped", since sf reads a layer in the dimension of its first geometry.

sample_points

Optional sf POINT cloud for k-means clustering. Method "random" places its seeds in boundary and does not read it; it is ignored there with a warning. Only the first two coordinate columns are clustered, so a Z or M dimension does not join the distance calculation and dominate it; rows without a location (an empty point, a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150, or in a geographic CRS a latitude beyond 90 degrees, read as given before any move) are dropped with a warning, so they never reach stats::kmeans(), which fails on them without naming a cause. A lon/lat cloud, or one with no CRS whose coordinates look like lon/lat (the heuristic ensure_projected() applies, with its warning), is projected before clustering. A cloud that mixes XY and XYZ (or XYM) points is read without Z and M before it is projected or clustered, since sf reads a layer in the dimension of its first geometry.

kmeans_nstart

The number of starts, of which the best is kept. NULL (default) uses 3 starts for partition = "density" and 10 for partition = "kmeans". Under partition = "kmeans" from random starts it is nstart of stats::kmeans(). A fresh partition is not the one resolution_profile() scored a count on; pass the selection or profile itself as n for that one (see n). Under partition = "density", and with init = "kmeans++", it has to be NULL or a positive whole number, so a number that is not whole, which partition = "kmeans" takes, stops a call that names no kind. It is not read by method = "random" or "provided".

kmeans_iter

Integer; iter.max for stats::kmeans(). Default 100 for both kinds (voronoi_seeds_kmeans() uses 50 for plain k-means by default). Under partition = "density" it is the most steps of Lloyd's iteration a start takes. Under partition = "density", and with init = "kmeans++", it has to be a positive whole number, and a kept start that was cut off at it is a warning of class "spatialkit_not_converged" (partition = "kmeans" from random starts keeps the warning stats::kmeans() gives).

set_seed

Optional integer seed for the random draws. Default NULL: the draws come from the session's random-number stream, so set.seed() before the call makes it reproducible. A number gives the same seeds every time and leaves the caller's stream as it was. (voronoi_seeds_kmeans() defaults to 456 instead.)

partition

For method = "kmeans": what the seeds minimise. "density" (default) is the sum of squared distances from the points of the cloud to their nearest seed, each point weighted by its local density to the power density_power: compact cells, many small ones where the points are dense and a few large ones where they are sparse. At the default power they hold about the same number of points each once n is above the number of dense places (clusters) in the cloud; below that the counts are about as uneven as under "kmeans". "kmeans" is the same sum unweighted: compact cells, with several times the points in a cell of a dense place that a cell of a sparse place holds. It is stats::kmeans() from 10 random starts on the rows as they come, with the coordinates centred, divided by the diagonal of their bounding box and rounded to 2^-30 of it, so that the seeds do not move with the unit or the origin; where the locations span less than a kilometre a change of unit or origin can still move them (see "The partition" in resolution_profile()). The density kind follows the density of sample_points; a cloud this function draws inside boundary is uniform and has none to follow. Without the FNN package the density kind finds its weights by comparing every pair of distinct locations, so its time grows with the square of their number; the seeds are the same, and nothing stops the call. See "The partition" in resolution_profile() for what each kind does and how.

init

For method = "kmeans": how each start is drawn, "random" (n distinct locations at random, as stats::kmeans() draws them) or "kmeans++" (the seeds one at a time, each in proportion to its squared distance from those already drawn, times its weight under partition = "density"). NULL (default) is each kind's own rule: "random" for partition = "kmeans" and "kmeans++" for partition = "density". Under partition = "kmeans" from random starts the cloud is clustered in the order its rows come in; with init = "kmeans++", and under partition = "density", the rows are put in coordinate order first, so the seeds do not depend on their order.

density_power

For partition = "density": the power the local density is raised to for a point's weight, from 0 to 2. Default 1, which evens out the cell counts once the cells outnumber the dense places; 0 weights every point alike. Setting it under partition = "kmeans" is a warning.

density_k

For partition = "density": the number of nearest neighbours the local density is read from. Default 8.

Value

An sf POINT object with seed_id and method columns. With method = "kmeans" it also carries attr(, "kmeans"), the run behind the seeds: cluster (the seed_id each clustered cloud point was assigned to), rows (those points' positions in the cloud, since rows with unusable coordinates are dropped first), size (points per seed), withinss and tot_withinss (the within-cluster sums of squares), iter and nstart. For the scored centres of a selection or profile (see n) it describes sample_points assigned to them, each point to its nearest seed, with iter NA and nstart the profile's restarts, and is absent when no sample_points were given. A point the same distance from two seeds (squared distances within one part in ten million) goes to the lower seed_id, the rule the profile scores its cells by, so the record is the same in another unit or with another origin. Under partition = "density" withinss and tot_withinss count every point once, about its cell's mean. A run this call makes with partition = "density" or init = "kmeans++" also records converged, whether the kept start stopped before kmeans_iter, and under partition = "density" objective, the weighted sum the seeds minimise; scored centres have neither. Seeds placed with partition = "density" or init = "kmeans++", and the scored centres of a profile of the density kind or from random starts, carry attr(, "partition"): a list with kind, init, density_power and density_k, and for seeds this call placed iter, iter_max and converged (the iterations the kept start took, the limit, and whether it stopped before the limit). build_tessellation() returns the list as params$partition. Seeds with no such record are plain k-means: from random starts when this call placed them, or the scored centres of a k-means profile from k-means++ starts. Every method also attaches attr(, "cover") when the call says what ground the seeds stand for (see "Details"): an sfc holding the boundary's polygons or the hull of the clustered points, in its own CRS.

When n is a select_resolution() result that carries count_rule, or a profile built with an estimate or read by cp, the seeds carry that record as attr(, "count_rule"): how the count was set, for which cell value, and what the profile scored at it. Its scored_cells is TRUE for the scored centres method = "kmeans" hands on, and FALSE for centres refitted to every point (see n) and for seeds this call places itself at that count: a k-means of its own when the selection holds no centres at the count, and every method = "random" seeding. method = "provided" does not read n and writes no record; seeds that already carry one (sel$seeds) keep it, marked FALSE when their number is not the record's count. build_tessellation() and assign_features_to_polygons() hand the record on, and summarize_by_cell() checks its result against it. A count given as a number, or read off a profile without an estimate by cp or elbow, has no record.

Details

Seeds lie inside the ground they stand for (k-means seeds inside the hull of the points they were fitted to, random seeds inside the boundary), so Voronoi cells clipped to the seeds' own hull would leave its edge uncovered. The result therefore carries that ground as attr(, "cover"): the boundary when one was given, otherwise the convex hull of sample_points (for lon/lat points, the hull of their coordinates in degrees, with the longitudes of points on both sides of 180 degrees taken from 0 to 360, -170 as 190), otherwise (for the scored centres of a resolution_profile() or a select_resolution() result passed as n) the hull of the points the profile was computed on. build_tessellation() and create_voronoi_polygons() derive their default boundary from it, so build_tessellation(seeds, method = "voronoi") holds every observation without a boundary. Seeds with no cover are tessellated over their own hull unless a boundary or cover is passed then: method = "provided" seeds given with neither boundary nor sample_points have none, and no warning is raised for them, since they may be the observation sites themselves. The attribute survives sf::st_transform() and row subsetting; rbind() drops it.

A k-means seed is a mean of the points of its cluster, weighted under the density kind, so it can lie outside a boundary that is not convex, in a bay or a bend of a coast, even when every point lies inside. Tessellated within that boundary, its cell is built if any of it lies inside: the part of the study area nearer the seed than any other seed. build_tessellation() gives the seed that cell in index, as it gives every seed the cell it generates, so seeds$cell_id <- tess$index holds each seed's cell for cell_values_at(). A seed with every part of the study area nearer another seed has no cell, NA in index, and a warning of class spatialkit_unassigned gives the number.

Sampling inside the boundary

Seeds drawn by method = "random", and the cloud method = "kmeans" draws when no sample_points are given, are sampled inside boundary. Its rows are repaired with sf::st_make_valid() before they are unioned. In longitude and latitude the union runs with s2, and a row s2 still refuses (crossing edges, a vertex listed twice) is repaired again, with crossing edges split as GEOS splits them in a projected CRS; a row s2 refuses even then stops the call with an error of class "spatialkit_cells_degenerate" that names it and says to transform boundary to a projected CRS.

In longitude and latitude, a boundary whose bounding box is over 10,000 times its area (small pieces far apart), which sf does not sample whole, is sampled piece by piece, the points shared among the pieces in proportion to their areas; a piece whose own box is over 10,000 times its area stops the call with an error that says to transform boundary to a projected CRS. A boundary whose bounding box has no height or no width (three vertices on one parallel) is refused. In longitude and latitude s2 reads the edges as great circles, which leave the bounding box read from the coordinates, and sf (without lwgeom) draws in that box: a boundary whose box has less than half its area on the sphere (three vertices on or near one parallel) is refused too. That error, and the error for a box with no height whose vertices lie on one parallel other than the equator, say to transform boundary to a projected CRS in which a parallel is a curve, such as the one ensure_projected() picks for it (a polar one, such as EPSG:3413 or 3031, for a ring around a pole), where the region has an area and lies in its box.

sf draws the points in the bounding box and keeps those inside, so it draws the number asked for times the ratio of the box to the area. In any CRS, a boundary that would take more than 10^6 points drawn in its box, or 10 times the points asked for if more (small pieces far apart, a thin strip at a slant), is sampled piece by piece in the same way (or whole, in draws of at most 10^6 points in its box, where that takes less time), and a piece that would still take more is drawn in such draws. Where the points drawn in all would exceed 2e7 (or 10 times the points asked for, if more), the call stops before any draw with an error that gives the ratio and says to pass sample_points (method = "kmeans", whose cloud is max(2000, 50 * n) points) or to ask for fewer seeds.

See also

Other cell building: build_tessellation(), clip_target_for(), create_grid_polygons(), create_grid_polygons_cached(), create_voronoi_polygons(), ensure_stable_poly_id(), plot_tessellation_map(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(), voronoi_seeds_random()

Examples

library(sf)
bnd <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(
  c(0, 0), c(100, 0), c(100, 100), c(0, 100), c(0, 0)
))), crs = 32632))
get_voronoi_seeds(bnd, method = "random", n = 5, set_seed = 1)
#> Simple feature collection with 5 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 20.16819 ymin: 6.178627 xmax: 90.82078 ymax: 94.46753
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 32N
#>   seed_id method                  geometry
#> 1       1 random POINT (26.55087 89.83897)
#> 2       2 random POINT (37.21239 94.46753)
#> 3       3 random POINT (57.28534 66.07978)
#> 4       4 random  POINT (90.82078 62.9114)
#> 5       5 random POINT (20.16819 6.178627)

# Seeds from a cloud with one dense place: density-weighted k-means (the
# default, 3 starts) against plain k-means.  The fewest and most points a
# seed's cell holds under each kind, with more seeds than dense places:
set.seed(2)
cloud <- st_as_sf(data.frame(x = c(rnorm(150, 30, 5), runif(50, 0, 100)),
                             y = c(rnorm(150, 30, 5), runif(50, 0, 100))),
                  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)
dens <- get_voronoi_seeds(bnd, method = "kmeans", n = 20,
                          sample_points = cloud, set_seed = 1)
km   <- get_voronoi_seeds(bnd, method = "kmeans", n = 20,
                          sample_points = cloud, set_seed = 1,
                          partition = "kmeans")
sizes <- list(density = attr(dens, "kmeans")$size,
              kmeans  = attr(km, "kmeans")$size)
sapply(sizes, range)   # fewest and most points per seed
#>      density kmeans
#> [1,]       6      1
#> [2,]      13     32
